coelophysis:enwiki:7.title: Coelophysis (Formerly assigned material and taxa, part 2)

facts.statement: The type species Coelophysis bauri was described by Edward Drinker Cope in 1889.
facts.quote: The type species C. bauri, originally placed in the genus Coelurus by Edward Drinker Cope in 1887, was described by the latter in 1889.

facts.statement: Megapnosaurus was once considered a species of Coelophysis, but it is now recognized as a valid separate genus.
facts.quote: Megapnosaurus was once considered to be a species within this genus, but this interpretation has been challenged and the genus Megapnosaurus is now considered valid.

facts.statement: It is debated whether scattered fossil material found worldwide in Late Triassic and Early Jurassic formations belongs to Coelophysis or similar animals.
facts.quote: Scattered material representing similar animals has been found worldwide in some Late Triassic and Early Jurassic formations.

facts.statement: Excavations at Ghost Ranch revealed a fossil layer containing hundreds of Coelophysis skeletons in a single concentration.
facts.quote: it was understood that the fossil layer contained hundreds of skeletons of Coelophysis in a single concentration

facts.statement: Excavations at the Ghost Ranch Coelophysis quarry continued through 1947 and 1948 by the American Museum of Natural History crew.
facts.quote: Excavations of the Ghost Ranch Coelophysis quarry were continued throughout 1947 and 1948 by the crew of the AMNH

facts.statement: The Ghost Ranch quarry was reopened and worked between 1981 and 1982, yielding 16 large blocks weighing between 6 and 10 short tons each.
facts.quote: The quarry was worked from 1981 to 1982, with 16 large blocks of 6 to 10 short ton excavated

facts.statement: Edwin H. Colbert published a monograph on Coelophysis in 1989.
facts.quote: A monograph on Coelophysis was then published by Colbert in 1989

facts.statement: All material from Ghost Ranch was described by Colbert as belonging to a single species of Coelophysis known from hundreds of individuals.
facts.quote: All of the Ghost Ranch material was thus described as part of a single species known from hundreds of individuals of various ages and sizes

facts.statement: While Colbert considered Coelophysis diagnostic, Richard Padian argued it was a 'metataxon' lacking unique characteristics due to its scrappy and incomplete original material.
facts.quote: Colbert considered Coelophysis to be diagnostic, this opinion was not shared in other reviews of early theropods, where Padian instead considered it a "metataxon" or otherwise lacking unique characteristics of its own

facts.statement: It is debated whether additional theropod material can be referred to Coelophysis, as Richard Padian argued the type material was too incomplete to justify such referrals.
facts.quote: Padian believed that as Coelophysis was founded in scrappy and incomplete material, it is difficult to justify the referrals of additional material to the taxon.

facts.statement: Coelophysis fossils from Ghost Ranch were found in the upper sandstone level of the Chinle Formation, which was believed to be Norian in age at the time of discovery.
facts.quote: All of the excavations at Ghost Ranch took place within the upper sandstone level of the Chinle Formation, believed to be Norian in age at the time

facts.statement: Specimens collected from Ghost Ranch between 1947 and 1982 were attributed to Coelophysis because they showed no differences beyond sexual or growth-related variation.
facts.quote: the Ghost Ranch specimens collected from 1947 to 1982 were referred to the taxon as they lacked differences beyond sexual or growth-related variation.

facts.statement: The complete skeleton AMNH 7224 was selected as the holotype for the proposed species Rioarribasaurus.
facts.quote: The complete skeleton AMNH 7224, mounted on display at the museum, was selected as the holotype of Rioarribasaurus

facts.statement: Paleontologists Hunt and Lucas designated the cervical vertebra AMNH 2701 as the lectotype for C. longicollis because the original type was invalid.
facts.quote: Hunt and Lucas also designated a lectotype for C. longicollis as the specimen chosen by Welles as its type was invalid, identifying that the cervical AMNH 2701 should be used to identify the species.

facts.statement: The partial ilium AMNH 2726 was designated as the lectotype for C. willistoni.
facts.quote: A lectotype was also designated for C. willistoni, the partial ilium AMNH 2726.

facts.statement: A 1996 study by Hunt, Lucas, Sullivan, and Heckert concluded that the locality where Baldwin collected Coelophysis was a different deposit than the dinosaur quarry originally identified by Colbert.
facts.quote: In a following study in 1996, Hunt and Lucas as well as American paleontologists Robert M. Sullivan and Andrew Heckert established that the locality where Baldwin collected Coelophysis was not the same deposit or level as the dinosaur quarry as Colbert had believed.

facts.statement: According to the stratigraphy proposed by Sullivan, Lucas, and colleagues, Coelophysis lived in the Revueltian-age Petrified Forest Formation while Rioarribasaurus lived in the Apachean-age Rock Point Formation.
facts.quote: According to the stratigraphy of Sullivan, Lucas and colleagues, Coelophysis would therefore be from the Revueltian-age Petrified Forest Formation, with Rioarribasaurus from the Apachean-age Rock Point Formation.

facts.statement: Material from relocated sites was used to argue that Coelophysis is distinct from Rioarribasaurus based on differences in the pubis, femur, and metatarsals.
facts.quote: Additional collected material from these relocated sites was used as justification for Coelophysis being a distinct taxon separated from Rioarribasaurus, showing differences in the pubis, femur, and metatarsals.

facts.statement: Hunt and Lucas believed that none of the material from three species possessed unique characteristics supporting their synonymy with C. bauri or other theropods.
facts.quote: None of the material of the three species was believed by Hunt and Lucas to bear any unique characteristics that could support their synonymy to C. bauri or any other theropod.

facts.statement: In 1993, paleoartist Gregory S. Paul opined that Coelophysis was indeterminate and that Rioarribasaurus and Syntarsus belonged to the same genus, proposing the combination Syntarsus colberti.
facts.quote: American paleoartist Gregory S. Paul also published in 1993 the opinion that Coelophysis was indeterminate, but that Rioarribasaurus and Syntarsus belonged to the same genus, creating the combination Syntarsus colberti.

facts.statement: The name Coelophysis was declared a nomen conservandum, resolving the confusion and uncertainty regarding its taxonomic status.
facts.quote: The name Coelophysis became a nomen conservandum ("conserved name"), and thus the confusion and uncertainty surrounding the status of Coelophysis was resolved.

facts.statement: In 1922, Case described the first material of Coelophysis found outside New Mexico, consisting of vertebrae collected in 1921 from the Dockum Formation in Crosby County, Texas.
facts.quote: In 1922 Case described the first supposed material of Coelophysis from outside New Mexico with the referral of a series of vertebrae he collected in 1921 from Dockum Formation of Crosby County, Texas.

facts.statement: In 1958, Colbert and Donald Baird rediscovered a specimen containing bone impressions of an early dinosaur, leading to comparisons suggesting it might be synonymous with Coelophysis.
facts.quote: Following the rediscovery of a specimen containing the bone impressions of an early dinosaur by Colbert and Donald Baird in 1958, Coelophysis was first compared to Podokesaurus as potentially synonymous.

facts.statement: Specimen BSNH No. 13656 was found in 1864 in possibly-Triassic sediments of Connecticut, likely the Portland Formation, and remained undescribed until Colbert and Baird worked on it.
facts.quote: BSNH No. 13656 was found in the in 1864 from possibly-Triassic sediments of Connecticut, probably the Portland Formation, and remained undescribed until the work of Colbert and Baird.

facts.statement: In 1983, a partial skeleton of a theropod was found at Cross Quarry in the Orphan Mesa region, a site named after its discoverer Robert Cross where Baldwin may have collected the original Coelophysis material.
facts.quote: In 1983 another partial skeleton of a theropod was found from the Orphan Mesa region where it is possible Baldwin collected the original Coelophysis material, at a site named Cross Quarry after its discoverer Robert Cross.

facts.statement: In 1999, Sullivan and Lucas named the specimen NMMNH P-22298 and material previously assigned to C. willistoni as Eucoelophysis after AMNH 7224 was designated the neotype of Coelophysis bauri.
facts.quote: Following the designation of AMNH 7224 as the neotype of Coelophysis bauri, C. longicollis, C. willistoni, and the specimens named C. bauri by Cope lacked a genus and species, so the NMMNH P-22298 as well as material previously assigned to C. willistoni (AMNH 2706) were named Eucoelophysis by Sullivan and Lucas in 1999.

facts.statement: In 2007, independent work by Sterling Nesbitt, Randall Irmis, and William Parker upheld the identification of Eucoelophysis as a silesaurid, distant from Coelophysis and the Baldwin material.
facts.quote: The identification of Eucoelophysis as a silesaurid, distant from Coelophysis and the Baldwin material, was upheld by independent work by American paleontologists Sterling Nesbitt, Randall Irmis and William Parker in 2007.

facts.statement: In 2024, a petition was submitted to the ICZN to retain Syntarsus as the name for the theropod.
facts.quote: In 2024, it has been petitioned to the ICZN that Syntarsus be retained for the name of the theropod.

facts.statement: In the 2000s, multiple authors provisionally considered S. rhodesiensis to be a species of Coelophysis, while S. kayentakatae was identified as belonging to a separate genus needing a new name.
facts.quote: Multiple authors in the 2000s provisionally considered S. rhodesiensis to be a species of Coelophysis, while S. kayentakatae has been identified as belonging to a separate genus and in need of a new name.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analyses of Coelophysidae found that S. rhodesiensis is not the sister taxon to Coelophysis, leading to the use of the name Megapnosaurus in those cases.
facts.quote: Phylogenetic analyses of Coelophysidae have found that S. rhodesiensis is not the sister taxon to Coelophysis, so the name Megapnosaurus has been used in those cases.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated the weight of Coelophysis at 15 kg for the gracile form, 20 kg for the robust form, and later 25 kg.
facts.quote: Gregory S. Paul (1988) estimated the weight of the gracile form at 15 kg and the weight of the robust form at 20 kg, but later presented a higher estimate of 25 kg.

facts.statement: Coelophysis was a bipedal, carnivorous theropod dinosaur that was a fast and agile runner.
facts.quote: Coelophysis was a bipedal, carnivorous, theropod dinosaur and a fast, agile runner.

facts.statement: Coelophysis bauri possessed a furcula, which is the earliest known example of this bone in a dinosaur.
facts.quote: C. bauri had a furcula (wishbone), the earliest known example in a dinosaur.

facts.statement: Coelophysis possessed four digits on its hand, with only three being functional and the fourth embedded in the flesh.
facts.quote: Coelophysis also preserves the ancestral condition of possessing four digits on the hand (manus). It had only three functional digits, with the fourth being embedded in the flesh of the hand.

facts.statement: The feet of Coelophysis ended in three toes with a raised dewclaw.
facts.quote: The leg ended in a three-toed foot (pes) with a raised dewclaw (hallux).

facts.statement: Coelophysis had a tail with interlocking vertebrae forming a semi-rigid lattice to prevent up-and-down movement.
facts.quote: The tail had an unusual structure within its interlocking prezygapophysis of its vertebrae, which formed a semi-rigid lattice, apparently to stop the tail from moving up and down.

facts.statement: Coelophysis had a long, narrow head approximately 270 mm long with large, forward-facing eyes providing excellent depth perception.
facts.quote: Coelophysis had a long and narrow head (approximately 270 mm), with large, forward-facing eyes that afforded it stereoscopic vision and, as a result, excellent depth perception.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Coelophysis bauri is the same species as Megapnosaurus rhodesiensis, with many paleontologists refuting the idea.
facts.quote: Several paleontologists consider Coelophysis bauri to be the same dinosaur as Megapnosaurus rhodesiensis (formerly Syntarsus). However, this has been refuted by many paleontologists.

facts.statement: Downs (2000) concluded that Coelophysis bauri differs from Megapnosaurus rhodesiensis in cervical length, leg proportions, and caudal vertebral anatomy.
facts.quote: Downs (2000) concluded that C. bauri differs from C. rhodesiensis in cervical length, proximal and distal leg proportions, and proximal caudal vertebral anatomy.

facts.statement: Bristowe and Raath (2004) concluded that Coelophysis bauri has a longer maxillary tooth row than Megapnosaurus rhodesiensis.
facts.quote: Bristowe and Raath (2004) concluded that C. bauri differs from M. rhodesiensis in having a longer maxillary tooth row.

facts.statement: Barta et al. (2018) concluded that Coelophysis bauri possesses a 5th metacarpal, distinguishing it from Megapnosaurus rhodesiensis.
facts.quote: Barta et al. (2018) concluded that C. bauri differed from M. rhodesiensis in that it bears its 5th metacarpal.

facts.statement: Griffin (2018) concluded that Coelophysis bauri differs from Megapnosaurus rhodesiensis in the musculature of the limbs.
facts.quote: Griffin (2018) concluded that C. bauri differs from M. rhodesiensis in several differences in the musculature of the limbs.

facts.statement: The type species C. bauri was described by Edward Drinker Cope in 1889.
facts.quote: La especie tipo, C. bauri, fue descrita por Edward Drinker Cope en 1889.

facts.statement: It lived during the late Triassic and early Jurassic, approximately 203 to 196 million years ago, in North America and Africa.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Triásico y a principios del Jurásico, hace aproximadamente 203 a 196 millones de años, desde el Noriense al Pliensbachiense en Norteamérica y África.

facts.statement: Its generic name refers to the hollow bones in its legs, derived from Greek words meaning "hollow" and "form".
facts.quote: Su nombre genérico se debe a que los huesos de sus patas eran huecos y proviene del griego antiguo κοιλος/koilos que significa "hueco" y φυσις/physis "forma".

facts.statement: Paul estimated the weight of the gracile form at 15 kilograms and the robust form at 20 kilograms in 1988.
facts.quote: Paul en 1988 estimó el peso de la forma grácil a 15 kilogramos, y el de la forma robusta a 20 kilogramos.

facts.statement: It was a slender, agile, carnivorous bipedal runner.
facts.quote: Este esbelto y ágil bípedo corredor carnívoro.

facts.statement: Two forms, robust and gracile, were originally thought to be different species but were later concluded to be males and females of the same species, C. bauri.
facts.quote: Fueron identificadas dos formas de celofisis, una robusta y otra grácil; al principio se consideró que se trataba de dos especies diferentes, pero más tarde los paleontólogos concluyeron que se trataba de machos y hembras de la misma especie, C. bauri.

facts.statement: It had narrow hips, forelimbs adapted for grasping, and narrow feet.
facts.quote: Coelophysis tenía caderas estrechas, extremidades anteriores adaptadas para agarrar y pies estrechos.

facts.statement: It retained the ancestral condition of having four digits in the hand, with only three functional digits and the fourth embedded in the flesh.
facts.quote: Coelophysis también conserva la condición ancestral de poseer cuatro dígitos en la mano. Tenía solo tres dígitos funcionales, el cuarto incrustado en la carne de la mano.

facts.statement: The hind limb ended in a three-toed foot with an elevated hallux.
facts.quote: La extremidad posterior terminó en un pie de tres dedos, con un hallux elevado.

facts.statement: Rinehart et al. concluded in 2004 that Coelophysis was a diurnal, vision-oriented predator based on a complete scleral ring found in a juvenile specimen.
facts.quote: Rinehart et al. en 2004 describieron el anillo esclerótico completo encontrado para un C. bauri juvenil, el espécimen NMMNH P-4200, y lo compararon con datos sobre los anillos escleróticos de reptiles y aves y concluyeron que Coelophysis era un depredador diurno orientado a la vista.

facts.statement: Its eyes appear most similar to those of eagles and hawks, with high accommodation power.
facts.quote: Los ojos de Coelophysis parecen ser los más cercanos a los de águilas y halcones, con un alto poder de acomodación.

facts.statement: The tail had an unusual structure in the prezygapophyseal joints forming a semi-rigid lattice, seemingly allowing movement only up and down.
facts.quote: La cola tenía una estructura inusual en las uniones prezigapofisis de sus vértebras, que formaban un enrejado semirrígido, para al parecer permitir que la cola se moviera sólo hacia arriba o hacia abajo.

facts.statement: This tail structure may have acted as a rudder or counterweight to help the animal maneuver at high speeds.
facts.quote: Esto al actuar como un timón o contrapeso puede haber ayudado cuando el animal maniobraba a gran velocidad.

facts.statement: The name Rioarribasaurus is a synonym of Coelophysis.
facts.quote: El nombre Rioarribasaurus es sinónimo de Coelophysis.

facts.statement: Other dinosaurs such as Podokesaurus and Megapnosaurus are considered synonyms of Coelophysis.
facts.quote: Otros dinosaurios como Podokesaurus y Megapnosaurus, son considerados como sinónimo de Coelophysis.

facts.statement: The genus existed from the Norian to the Sinemurian, between 227.3 and 192.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Norian to Sinemurian (227.3 to 192.9 million years ago)
